decisionsTitle: The route's checkpoints: «Tradu din română» on the GPX names, the profile across the page with a dotted line at each point, no closing clock before the gun time, the fork over the drop
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-17, 18:40–19:05, of the route's checkpoints card, the elevation profile and the page's table «Puncte de control» (§757, §802, §805):** five asks, none a new rule. 1. «Aici îmi lipsește traducerea automată» — the English names of the points the GPX offered had no «Tradu din română». 2. «This needs to span across the entire width of the screen» — the profile left the right of a wide screen empty. 3. «I want a dotted vertical line across the chart to show exactly where these points are». 4. «Asta nu e corect pentru că încă nu știm exact la ce oră dăm startul cursei» — the table said «se închide la 12:00» for a race whose gun time was not set. 5. «Și dacă am apă și hrană, trebuie arătată iconița de hrană, pentru că aia e mai valoroasă; apa e cumva implicită dacă avem mâncare».

**Decision, amending §464, §757, §802 and §805; no migration.**

**«Tradu din română» beside every checkpoint English name (amends §464, §757).** The house's `TranslateFieldButton` stands under the English name of every row the GPX's preview offers and under the English name and the English note of every saved and every spare row of the list; absent, as everywhere, where the deployment offers no translation. The button finds its box by the pair's spelling (`translate/domain/fields.ts`) and, outside a form that owns the box, by name on the page — and the preview and the list's saved rows are two forms on one page. So the preview's boxes are renamed `gp[<n>].nameRo` / `gp[<n>].nameEn` (they were `cp[<n>].…`, the same names as the list's rows, which a button would have resolved to whichever stood first). The action that adds the ticked points reads the new names (`posted.ts#postedGpxPicks`), says a refusal's boxes in the same spelling (`gpxPreviewFields`), and the refusal summary has the two labels. The allowlist gains `cp[<n>].nameEn`, `cp[<n>].noteEn` and `gp[<n>].nameEn`; the card has no «Tradu cardul: RO → EN» (its boxes belong to detached forms, which the card press does not read, and the card has no language tabs; the volunteers' card has the one precedent) — that is a follow-up, not a gap in this change.

**The profile spans the page (amends §802).** The page draws three fixed frames, shown by CSS alone and each at `width: 100%` of the section with no cap but the phone's 480 px: narrow (360 × 240, labels 14 units, under 700 px), wide (1000 × 280, labels 19 units, from 700 to 1099 px) and full (1600 × 320, labels 19 units, from 1100 px). The event page's container is the theme's `xl` (2040 px) less the gutters (16 px under 600 px, 24 px above), so the chart is up to 1992 px wide, and the labels read 12.4 px at 700 px of screen, 20 px at 1099, 12.5 px at 1100, 14.6 px at 1280, 22.2 px at 1920 and 23.7 px at the container's cap — between 12 and 24 px on every screen, which one frame as wide as the screen could not promise without measuring the browser (a Server Component cannot). The pointer island reads whichever chart is showing. The race number's strip does not draw from this component and is untouched.

**A dotted line at every checkpoint (amends §802).** On the narrow, wide and full charts a one-pixel dotted line runs from the base of each pin straight down to the kilometre axis at the point's exact kilometre, in the pin's own muted colour (`--mui-palette-text-secondary`; no new token), under the curve's tint so the curve stays readable; it replaces the short solid stem (the dotted line passes through the same point), and the pin, its glyph and the small dot on the curve stay. Two pins at one kilometre share one line. The editor's small preview keeps its short stems.

**No closing clock while the race's gun time is not set (amends §757).** A clock is a promise about the gun: `start.ts#cutoffClockStart` is `checkpointStart` except that a race whose `race_starts_at` is null has none, so `withCutoffClocks`, `checkpointClock` and the finish row's `limit` leave the clock null. The page's table says «Timp limită: 2 h» for every point and for «Sosire» (the finish row stays, with its duration alone — `checkpointRows` no longer needs the clock to draw it), the editor's aside says `cutoffAside` without the clock, and the race number's strip prints no «km 12 · 11:30» for it. The minutes are unchanged and still counted from the event's start while the gun is open (`checkpointStart`, `raceTimeLimitMinutes`), and the «Timp limită» line under «Traseu» (§798) and «Când» (`whenTimes`, «Ora startului cursei se anunță») are as they were. A race whose gun time equals the event's start has it set and keeps its clocks; every other event type has no gun and counts from its own start. Nothing to invalidate: the page derives the clocks from the event row at render (`withCutoffClocks(checkpoints, dated)`), so a gun time set later is the same save that moves the event, and the bib's picture stamp already carries `race_starts_at` beside each limit (`CHECKPOINTS_STAMP`), so the picture address changes with it.

**The food glyph wins on a pin (amends §802).** The one glyph a pin draws is chosen in `geometry.ts#glyphForKinds`; with the new option `foodBeforeWater` the order is food, water, first aid, timing, direction — a point with «Mâncare» and «Apă» pins the fork, water alone the drop, the other kinds as before. The page's chart and the editor's preview pass it. The race number's strip draws from the same core without it and keeps its glyphs (a cup for water, a fork for food alone, a dot otherwise, §804): changing it moves `BIB_DRAWING_VERSION`, so it follows at the strip's next drawing version.

**Refused.** One frame as wide as the screen, measured in the browser (a client island and a flash of the wrong size, for labels that a fixed frame keeps legible). A second tick for the dotted lines. A card-wide translate press on the checkpoints card in this change. Changing the race number's strip in this change.
changelogLine: - **Checkpoints and the elevation profile, five small asks** — «Tradu din română» beside the GPX points' English names (and the list's names and notes); the profile spans the page's width; a dotted line marks each checkpoint's kilometre; no «se închide la» while the race's start is not set; a point with food and water shows the fork. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criteria 82 and 83. Given an event whose route has a GPX with altitudes, when its page renders, then the profile is drawn as a narrow chart (under 700 pixels, at most 480 pixels wide), a wide one (700 to 1099 pixels) and a full one (from 1100 pixels), each the width of the page's content with no other cap, CSS showing the one that fits, so its labels are 11 pixels or more from 320 pixels and between 12 and 24 pixels from 700 pixels up; a dotted vertical line one pixel thin runs from each pin down to the kilometre axis at the point's exact kilometre, under the curve, one line for two pins at one kilometre; and a point with «Mâncare» and «Apă» pins the fork, a point with «Apă» alone the drop, the editor's preview drawing the same glyphs (2026-10-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criteria 79 and 82. Given a race whose gun time is not set («Startul cursei nu e stabilit»), when its page renders, then a checkpoint's line and the finish row read «Timp limită: 2 h» («Time limit: 2 h») with no «se închide la» («closes at») and the finish row is still there; once the gun time is set, or equals the event's start, the clocks return; any other event type counts its clocks from its own start; the editor's aside says the duration alone while the gun time is not set (2026-10-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 20. Given the event editor's «Puncte de control», when the deployment offers translation, then «Tradu din română» stands under the English name of every point the GPX's preview offers and under the English name and the English note of every saved and every spare row, translating from the Romanian twin as the other buttons do and saving nothing; the preview's boxes are named apart from the list's rows (`gp[n]`, `cp[n]`) so a button finds its own box, and without a translator no button is drawn (2026-10-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 97. Given a race whose gun time is not set, when a number is printed or previewed with «…cu orele limită», then its strip prints no clock for a checkpoint, «km 12» alone; the strip's glyphs are unchanged by the page's food-before-water order (2026-10-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the GPX points' English names get «Tradu din română», the elevation profile spans the page's width, a dotted line marks every checkpoint's km, the food glyph wins on a pin, no closing clock while the race's start is not set
